newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia king says will not abdicate.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia king says will not abdicate.

text.p: Cambodian King Norodom Sihanouk on Monday said he had decided not to abdicate and vowed to stay out of politics after his planned return to his troubled Southeast Asian homeland this month.

Sihanouk said he had been urged to renounce his throne by opponents of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who seized power in Cambodia in July, and that he himself wanted to abdicate but had decided that to do so would be to abandon his people.
"After having weighed the pros and cons for many nights, I decide to remain as king for some time longer," Sihanouk said in a statement faxed to reporters.

"To abdicate at this time, when my people have so much need of the comfort of my presence near them...to abdicate, I said, would be to abandon them, to desert them," said the king, who has been receiving medical treatment in Beijing.
"This is something that a king worthy of the name does not do," he said.

Sihanouk reigns but does not rule in Cambodia, and opponents of Hun Sen's ousting of the king's son First Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh have suggested he could abdicate to clear the way for a return to politics.
The king repeated a pledge to return to Cambodia in August but said he planned to stay in the northwestern town of Siem Reap, home of the famed Angkor Wat temple complex.
"I will return to Cambodia before the end of this month to live in Siem Reap-Angkor, far from the politicians of Phnom Penh," he said.
"Until my death, I will continue to serve...my country and my people, but not in the political arena," he said.
